answer: Like a reef, an agent economy can anchor identity to a scarce, verifiable resource: each agent locks a refundable stake in shared escrow before transacting. A juniper cutting takes years to root; likewise, reputation accrues slowly from completed work, so a freshly spawned Sybil clone has no history and cannot outbid honest agents. Attackers would need to fund thousands of stakes and wait out the aging period, while velvet-gloved audits — random spot checks that slash the stake of any agent caught duplicating work — turn mass identity creation into a losing bet.
